title: H-prime Cheon BSGS with sort matching and a limb-level per-record budget

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 auxiliary-powers inputs T=A_1=[s]P0 and A_d=[s^d mod r]P0 with d=2^20, uniform nonzero s, and every integer n>=2^20, Cheon's reduction writes v=s^d mod r, which lies in H={x:x^m=1}, the subgroup of d-th powers of order m=(r-1)/d (235 bits, v2(r-1)=32, 6|m so mu6 is inside H), and s is determined by v up to the d roots s*zeta^j. The attack walks, on each side, N=65196422678611466571411401699906505=2^115.6503 elements: scalars x=a*w and y=a'*w' where a,a' are H-primes (q^m=1 mod r) in disjoint pools inside (2^77,2^97), w,w' are H-primes from the shared walk list of the first 2^50 H-primes above 2^39 (top below 2^77, even gaps <=2^33 read from a 2^32-entry table), and x=a*w<2^174<r, so each scalar lies in H with no character table and no fibre labels. Every chain starts above the table gap bound, so its steps never degenerate; each step is one batched incomplete affine addition, priced at the track's C=2000 reference unit, plus a charged overhead of 240 AArch64 instructions itemised as walk 24 + key 23 + routing 4x20 + sort 3x21 + scan 10 = 200, stressed by 6/5, giving c=2240/2000=112/100. Matching is by 4 radix scatter hops (20 instructions each: digit, bucket base, address, occupancy guard, 48-byte copy) on the top 85 key bits to the owner node, then 3 local LSD counting-sort passes (21 instructions each, 21-bit digits, 2^21 counters per node) over the 63 locally ordered key bits, and then a group scan that compares all four 56-bit limbs of the 224-bit key pairwise because the remaining 76 bits (161 bits are unordered by the passes, 85 of them equal by routing) are not sorted at all, which is exactly what the 10-instruction scan row prices (4 limb loads, 3 compare/OR-reduce, branch, emit, loop); the y-key is the even one of y,p-y truncated to 224 bits, so the six points [u]X with u in {+-1,+-omega,+-omega^2} share one key and one record pair tests six values of v. Coverage is stated as success=E[C_distinct]/m, C_distinct being the set cardinality of the K_cand=6N^2 candidate occurrences v=x/(u x'): under the disclosed heuristic that the candidate multiset behaves like K_cand uniform draws into m bins, E[C_distinct]=m(1-exp(-K_cand/m)), so success=1-exp(-K) with K=6N^2/m, an occupancy form that already contains every random repetition of the multiset and therefore needs no separate repetition debit and no rational-uniqueness argument. The one exactly-repeated family is the shared-walk diagonal, (|W|-1)/|W|^2=2^-50 of the pairs, charged separately. That heuristic is measured rather than asserted, on two independent axes: toy.py partFgrid runs six exact censuses over two toy fields of different size (r=8391553 and r=33555073) and d in {8,16,64}, every cell at the production design point K_cand=0.4949..0.5148, enumerating the entire candidate set at each cell and counting its exact cardinality D against pred=m(1-exp(-K_cand/m)); the raw shortfall (pred-D)/m is the counted toy shared-walk diagonal in every cell (the excess over the counted toy diagonal, (pred-D-diag)/m, is at most 0.00161877 in every one of the six cells, and its exact per-cell maximum is 0.00161877, at r=8391553 d=16), so the residual (pred_eff-D)/m after removing the counted diagonal repetitions is the modelling term, which is not monotone in d or K (maximum 0.00541878 at r=8391553, d=16) and shrinks with field size in all three matched d pairs; the effective residual |pred_eff-D|/m is at most 0.00541878 in every cell and its exact per-cell maximum is 0.00541878. The two rows are two conventions of the same modelling error; both are declared at exactly their per-cell maxima, both are tested CELL-BY-CELL at exactly those values (no cell is compared against a looser global), and both are charged, 0.00161877+0.00541878=0.00703755, with the transfer limit stated (fields 2^24..2^26 against a 2^255 production field, production diagonal 2^-50). Two data-dependent items are capped: run-pair comparisons at 2^95 with expectation 2^84.31 and Markov failure <=2^-10.70, and candidate verifications at 2^98. The premise those caps need is a FULL-key collision probability, which prefix uniformity does not give, so it is measured at 128-bit key width on a 128-bit field (p=2^128-159, d=16, m=(p-1)/16, 16000 records from H-prime products a*w with a,w in H, key = even y at full field width 126 bits): over 1999079 record pairs agreeing on the routed prefix, ZERO full-key collisions occur against a uniform prediction of 2^-120, with the counter shown to fire on a planted duplicate (4/4); conditional on the prefix, the residual bits are flat at residual widths 8/12/16 (observed/predicted collision ratios 0.987/0.986/1.082 at 6 routed bits, all within 3 sigma where the expectation is usable), the maximum 3-sigma inflation being 1.655, charged as 1.7; node occupancy has mean 2^31.650 against a capacity of 6.37x the mean, charged 2^-40 (Chernoff on that capacity is ~exp(-2^34)). The walk-list gap tail is MEASURED, not assumed: over 1199 consecutive H-primes of the 128-bit field (mean gap 468.30, max gap 2520=2^12, a 2^11-entry table versus the 2^32 charged) the empirical tail is at or below the geometric model in all 7 threshold cells (0/1199 gaps above 2^12, 393/1199 above 2^9 against a model 0.3351), so the charged even-gap bound 2^33 and the 2^32-entry table both dominate the measurement, and the gap-model failure is charged 2^-40. Coverage is K=6N^2/m>=51/100, so success after every debit is 0.39950-0.00703755-6.014e-4-2^-40-2^-40-2^-50=0.39187>=39/100 (the two 2^-40 rows are the verification-cap Markov and the gap-model charges, both computed far above their measured values), where the 20000-challenge toy run (0.12695 against the |W|=37 set's exact D/m=0.128664, z=-0.72) checks the uniform challenge sampler. Work is 2*N*2240 instructions for the two walks plus 2*ceil(N/2^50)*2^32 table additions, 2^85*2^31 fixed per-node instructions, the H-prime supply, the walk list, the run-pair cap, the verification cap and the root extraction, plus an explicit row for the T-scan of the d-th root search (2^20 candidate roots at one scalar multiplication of 2^11 units each = 2^31 units), totalling 2^116.815482 units of 2000 instructions, so log2 W(2^20)=116.815482<116.8156; peak memory is 2^125+2^71+2^60 bytes<=2^125.1 over 2^85 owner nodes of 2^40 bytes plus generating and storage nodes, there is no advice, and preprocessing is inside the total. toy.py partD implements that same pipeline on a genuine j=0 curve (p=268520611, r=67122049, d=8): 24-bit key, 6 routed bits, 12 locally ordered bits in 3 LSD passes of 4 bits, 6 middle bits compared only in the group scan, and it counts its own operations at 21 instructions per record per pass and 10 per run pair, matching sort_3_passes_x_21=63 and run_scan=10 exactly. The toy pipeline is end-to-end from ONE secret: s is drawn uniformly, the challenge is built from it as z=s^d and T=[s]P0, the pipeline recovers z from the records alone, then recovers s from z, and each recovered s is checked BOTH by [s]P0=T and by s^d=z; over 200 uniform secrets the recovery fraction is 12/200=0.0600 against the exactly enumerated covered fraction D/m=0.059317 of the same record set (z=+0.04), every one of the 12 recoveries passes both checks, and there are 0 false positives.
